suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP Plugin Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug' — pipeline extracted zero detection rules for plugin exploitation or plugin-specific vulnerability signatures despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to vulnerable Gravity SMTP plugin endpoints (e.g., /wp-content/plugins/gravity-forms-smtp/, plugin-specific parameters). Monitor for exploit payload patterns associated with known CVEs affecting this plugin. Alert on HTTP 200 responses from exploit attempts followed by plugin-configuration file reads.

suggestion.title: API Key Exposure from Plugin Configuration Files
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Expose API Keys' — no detection rule covers extraction or leakage of credentials from plugin settings. This is the stated attack outcome and should anchor a detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file system access to Gravity SMTP plugin configuration directories and files (wp-content/plugins/gravity-forms-smtp/settings, database config backups). Alert on process reads of these paths followed by file copy, compression, or exfiltration-tool execution. Flag unusual process handles opening API credential storage.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SMTP API Credential Usage Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once API keys are exposed, attackers use them for unauthorized SMTP relay or spam campaigns — article does not describe post-exploitation behavior but this is the predictable follow-on attack and a critical detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate SMTP API calls associated with the Gravity SMTP service. Alert on API credentials being used from new geographic regions, at significantly higher request rates than baseline, or to send email to previously uncontacted domains. Flag API key usage after expected plugin maintenance windows or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Version Enumeration and Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires attacker knowledge of vulnerable plugin versions — no detection for reconnaissance/fingerprinting phase despite this being a prerequisite for targeted exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests that reveal plugin version numbers (readme.txt, plugin header comments, ?v=version query params) or requests to Gravity SMTP plugin pages that return version info in response headers. Alert on scanning patterns that enumerate multiple plugin versions or probe known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of WordPress Plugin Credentials Over Alternative Protocols
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies API keys were exposed and attackers accessed them — pipeline did not surface detection for credential exfiltration. Credentials could be transmitted via DNS, HTTPS C2, email, or data staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for base64-encoded or hex-encoded API credentials in outbound DNS queries, HTTPS POST bodies to suspicious domains, or email attachments. Alert on bulk file reads from plugin config directories followed by anomalous outbound traffic containing credential-like patterns (high entropy strings, known API key formats).

suggestion.title: Craft CMS actionResourceJs Host/X-Forwarded-Host header poisoning detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'an attacker can poison the Host or X-Forwarded-Host header to manipulate the application's $baseUrl.' This is the primary entry technique (T1190). No hunt explicitly detects malformed or attacker-controlled Host headers in requests to /actions/app/resource-js—UC_10_1 hunts volume, not header content anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for requests to /actions/app/resource-js where Host or X-Forwarded-Host header contains an external FQDN, differs from baseline legitimate domain by Levenshtein distance >2 characters, or contains suspicious markers (attacker-controlled TLD, .external, .test, private IP ranges). Establish baseline from 7-day clean-traffic window.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Service Endpoint Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploits 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — detection should monitor for HTTP/network requests to sidecar without authentication headers or tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk infrastructure for requests to PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints lacking Authorization headers or authentication context. Flag requests from untrusted sources or non-Splunk processes attempting to reach internal service ports. Splunk log source: _internal with 'sidecar' or service endpoint patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Process Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack capability: 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — filesystem operations by Splunk daemons outside approved paths/patterns indicate exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Splunk processes (spl_server, mongod, etc.) performing file write/delete operations outside /opt/splunk/* or other known-safe directories. Correlate with timestamp of exploit attempts. Windows: monitor WMI/PS events launching file operations; Linux: auditd rules on splunk process file syscalls.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies scanners are active; detect internal/external scanners identifying this CVE across the fleet. Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' — asset-exposure confirmation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Splunk Enterprise version detection or endpoint probes targeting CVE-2026-20253. Splunk: `index=_internal host=* version AND Enterprise | stats by host`. Defender KQL: DeviceInfo where OnboardingStatus=='Onboarded' | scan for Splunk product + version = vulnerable range.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Connectivity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector specifically references 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — abnormal network connections to sidecar or direct PostgreSQL access from non-Splunk processes signals exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections to PostgreSQL sidecar port (typically 5432 or custom) from sources outside trusted Splunk processes. Windows: monitor NetConnections for postgres port; Linux: netstat/ss monitoring or eBPF. Exclude normal Splunk internal connections; flag everything else.

suggestion.title: Service Endpoint Request Without Authentication Context
suggestion.rationale: Core exploitation: 'unauthenticated user' can call sidecar endpoints — look for successful HTTP responses (200/201) to service endpoints that previously returned 401/403 or vice versa, or requests lacking standard auth tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to service-related paths (e.g., /services/*, /sidecar/*, /admin/*) with no Authorization, X-Splunk-Authorization, or Bearer token headers, particularly returning 2xx. Splunk: `index=_access group=* method IN (POST, PUT, DELETE) | search auth=* | stats count by user, auth, uri`. Flag null or empty auth on critical endpoints.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection Attempts Against Service Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Argument Injection Vulnerability' — even if title/body mismatch, this pattern should be detected: monitor for special characters in service endpoint parameters (command separators, wildcards, path traversal sequences).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect payloads in HTTP request parameters to service endpoints containing injection metacharacters: `;`, `|`, `&`, `>`, `<`, `$()`, backticks, `../`, `\x00`. WAF should flag; if not WAF-visible, monitor application logs for malformed parameter parsing errors. Example: GET /sidecar?param=value;rm -rf /

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detection of external/internal access to this service endpoint without valid credentials is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically port 5432 or service-internal) for HTTP/network requests originating from external or untrusted networks. Flag any requests that lack authentication headers or pre-auth session tokens. Establish baseline of legitimate internal service-to-service traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as ability to 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Detection should monitor for unexpected file write/modification operations, especially in sensitive directories (config, binary, system).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation by Splunk processes (splunkd, python, etc.) in directories outside expected installation paths (/opt/splunk, /var/lib/splunk). Cross-correlate with endpoint authentication logs to identify requests originating from unauthenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Version Inventory Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch due date 2026-06-21. Standard vulnerability management: detect Splunk Enterprise instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253 (versions prior to patch release).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise endpoints reporting version < [patched version]. Cross-check against patch deployment logs to identify unpatched hosts. Given federal due date, escalate any unpatched instances in federal or regulated environments.

suggestion.title: Service Endpoint Access Pattern Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation of 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—an internal service. Detection should baseline normal service-to-service communication and alert on anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate internal traffic to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar. Alert on lateral movement or external scans probing this endpoint from unexpected source IPs/segments. Monitor for port scanning activity targeting common PostgreSQL ports on Splunk infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' and 'CVE: CVE-2026-20253.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being active exploitation (CISA KEV). This is the primary detection requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk Enterprise instances with versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference asset inventory against known-vulnerable release signatures. Federal patch deadline 2026-06-21; any unpatched instance post-deadline is confirmed exploitable in the wild.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exact attack surface — pipeline did not extract the endpoint pattern or exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/network requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints originating from external or unauthenticated sources. Splunk logs should show connection attempts and any authentication-bypass payloads. Look for database-write operations post-connection.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation from Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Pipeline missed the file-system impact detection entirely — this is the observable consequence of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation or truncation on Splunk instances, especially in sensitive directories (config, spool, data). Correlate file-write events from Splunk service accounts with prior failed authentication attempts or sidecar endpoint access. Flag deletions of audit logs or critical files.

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Port Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry implies active reconnaissance of exposed Splunk infrastructure. Article references 'public-facing application' exploitation (T1190). Pipeline must surface port-scanning activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multi-port scans targeting Splunk infrastructure from external IPs, particularly probing for open service ports (sidecar likely runs on high-numbered internal port). Flag successful connections followed by file-system or process activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states core attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this explicit operational detail.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/TCP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (5432 range or Splunk-specific variants) from external/untrusted networks lacking authentication headers (no Authorization, missing session tokens). Cross-reference against Splunk Enterprise asset inventory for CVE-2026-20253 vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Pattern — Arbitrary File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Kill-chain reconstruction is empty; no impact-phase detection suggested despite describing post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar access attempts with unexpected file create/delete/truncate operations on the Splunk host. Flag file operations in system directories or application-critical paths initiated without corresponding auth success.

suggestion.title: Asset-Exposure Hunt: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requests 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template substitution. Zero use cases generated despite article providing template reference and asking for Splunk SPL and Defender KQL. Federal due-date 2026-06-21 indicates urgent patch compliance check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Splunk Enterprise installations across fleet; match against patched version baseline for CVE-2026-20253. Flag any unpatched instances exposed to untrusted networks. Correlate with network logs for inbound connections to Splunk listening ports from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Reconnaissance and Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies PostgreSQL sidecar as attack surface. Pre-exploitation reconnaissance (port scanning, version enumeration) should be detected as early warning signal before file-operation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed connection attempts, port scans, or protocol probes targeting Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints. Look for rapid connection attempts across multiple ports from single source before successful exploitation sequence.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise: Unauthenticated Access to Critical Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user'—detect attempts to access protected endpoints without valid authentication. Operationalizes T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk access logs for requests to critical paths (/api/*, /services/*) from external IPs that lack Authorization headers or fail authentication validation. Alert on clusters of 401/403 responses followed by successful access from the same source—indicates reconnaissance then exploitation.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service: Unauthorized Connection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector is 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this internal service should not be accessible without internal authentication. Monitor for direct external access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections to PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or internal mappings) from external networks or untrusted internal hosts. Monitor postgres query logs for DDL operations (CREATE/DROP/TRUNCATE) initiated from Splunk application contexts that normally only execute SELECT/UPDATE.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Create/Truncate Operations from Splunk Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as ability to 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this is anomalous for a search/analytics platform. Detect scope deviation in file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file system events from Splunk daemon accounts for creation/truncation of files outside expected application directories (/opt/splunk, /var/log). Flag mass file deletion patterns, targeting of /etc or system binaries, or modification of Splunk configuration files via unauthorized paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Scanner Match and Patch Validation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active exploitation; article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—inventory all Splunk Enterprise instances and validate patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20253 matches across all Splunk deployments. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify vulnerable instances. Prioritize external-facing instances. Validate that patch versions released after 2026-06-21 have been deployed; alert on any externally-accessible Splunk instances running pre-patch versions.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise: External Network Accessibility Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article requires asset-exposure hunt; T1190 requires public-facing application. Enumerate and alert on exposed Splunk ports regardless of patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Conduct network scan for Splunk default ports (8000, 8089) accessible from untrusted networks. Audit firewall inbound rules for any that permit external access to Splunk. Cross-reference DNS A records and identify any CNAME/alias entries pointing to Splunk instances; validate all are intentional and behind WAF/VPN controls.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Splunk Enterprise Inventory (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution for CVE-2026-20253. CISA KEV entries mandate inventory as first detection step. Pipeline generated nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253 (check version against CVSS data). Prioritize Internet-facing instances. Confirm actual running version to catch patch-lag.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Sidecar API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. The exploitation path requires unauthenticated HTTP/API access to internal service ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Splunk sidecar/bootstrap API endpoints that succeed without prior authentication session. Monitor for POST/PUT/DELETE to file manipulation endpoints from external source IPs or anomalous user contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Operations via Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'. File creation/truncation executed via compromised Splunk daemon is the impact phase; truncating system files could disable logging, bypass auth, or trigger DoS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk daemon (splunkd) for suspicious file I/O: creation in /etc, /root, /var/log; truncation of critical system or Splunk files. Cross-correlate with unauthenticated API access 10-60 seconds prior to confirm exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Port Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. These internal service ports should not be Internet-routable; exposure is prerequisite for CVE-2026-20253 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall/network logs for inbound connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 9997, 8000, or custom) from untrusted external subnets. Correlate source IPs with intrusion intel and check for successful 3-way handshake (confirmed access).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the core attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints lacking authentication headers or valid credentials. Alert on connections to Splunk sidecar ports (8191 or custom) from external sources without prior authentication. Track 401/403 sequences followed by successful access as exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Operations via Compromised Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation manifests as 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—measurable via file system events as post-exploitation impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, truncation, or deletion from Splunk service accounts (splunkd, postgres sidecar process) targeting system directories (/etc, /var/spool, /usr/bin) or Splunk metadata paths. Establish baseline of expected operations; flag anomalies with high urgency.

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing Splunk Enterprise Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies 'active exploitation against exposed assets'—inventory of externally-reachable Splunk instances is prerequisite for risk quantification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query external vulnerability/port scan databases for Splunk Enterprise on standard ports (8000, 8089, 8191) reachable from internet. Cross-reference internal inventory against CVE-2026-20253 patch status. Prioritize instances with inbound connections from untrusted sources in the past 30 days.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Query Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: The sidecar is the exploitation pivot; successful attacks surface as unauthorized file-system queries or data modification through the service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar query logs for file-system operations (COPY, shell-exec equivalents, or unusual DDL on system tables). Correlate with network logs showing unauthenticated sidecar access. Flag any queries originating from non-Splunk processes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Authentication Header Analysis
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function'—tracking presence/absence of auth on sidecar requests reveals exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate unauthenticated sidecar access (if any exist) and alert on spike or new source IPs. Measure ratio of auth-missing to auth-present requests per endpoint. Trigger on sustained unauthenticated access followed by file operation events.

suggestion.title: Splunk Index Integrity Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: File truncation via sidecar could corrupt Splunk indexes or configuration—detectable via integrity monitoring and index validation queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk index file hashes and sizes for unexpected changes. Alert on index rebuild failures or corruption warnings in logs. Correlate timing of integrity violations with sidecar access logs to establish exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit the vulnerability through missing authentication on critical function. This is the initial attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated requests to Splunk critical function endpoints, particularly PostgreSQL sidecar service interfaces. Track 401/403 responses followed by successful access or repeated exploitation from same source.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the concrete impact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints for unexpected file creation/truncation operations on system or critical directories. Flag file operations initiated from unauthenticated or unexpected sources, especially targeting Splunk configuration or system files.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV means active wild exploitation. Article provides CVE explicitly as IOC; need signature-based detection for known exploitation patterns before legitimate patching occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy signatures for CVE-2026-20253 exploitation patterns (endpoint path traversal, parameter mutation targeting missing auth validation). Alert on any matches and correlate against vulnerability scanner confirmed-vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Vulnerability Hunting and Patch Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and explicitly references asset-exposure hunt template. Comprehensive hunt needed for exposed vulnerable instances regardless of scanner results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system for Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 presence. Hunt for exposed instances on public-facing infrastructure or with inadequate authentication controls. Compare patch deployment timeline against exploitation activity windows.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access Baselines and Alerting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint as the attack surface. Unauthorized access patterns to this specific component should trigger immediate alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected PostgreSQL sidecar access patterns by source, time, and operation type. Alert on connections from unexpected sources, unauthenticated attempts, or port scanning activity on PostgreSQL default ports within Splunk infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthorized Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can access PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint without authentication. This is the initial foothold: "allows an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint."
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connection attempts to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically localhost:5432 or internal service ports) from unauthenticated sources or external IPs. Alert on successful connections without prior authentication handshake. For network-exposed instances, flag any inbound connection to PostgreSQL sidecar ports from external addresses.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk PostgreSQL Service
suggestion.rationale: Core attack capability: "create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint." This manifests as impact-phase file system abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation events originating from Splunk PostgreSQL service processes (postgres.exe, postgres daemon). Baseline legitimate file operations; flag unexpected targets outside Splunk data/config directories. Critical: monitor for truncation of Splunk configuration, recovery, or system files that would degrade availability.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet-Facing Service Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV definition: "only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild" implies active targeting of exposed instances. Article context: Splunk is Internet-accessible and vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances listening on public IPs or accessible from untrusted networks. Validate network segmentation: PostgreSQL sidecar should never be reachable externally. Alert on any Splunk service responding to internet scans on standard web/database ports (8000, 8089, 5432).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempts — Failed Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Direct exploitation indicator: Article specifies 'missing authentication for critical function'—attackers will attempt to invoke database functions without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk/PostgreSQL logs for requests to sidecar endpoints (e.g., /services/admin) without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Flag repeated 401/403 errors followed by successful requests without intervention. Alert on database function calls that bypass Splunk's RBAC layer.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — must detect HTTP/API requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar without auth headers or with invalid session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints (typically :5432 or sidecar-specific ports) that lack authentication tokens, return 401 before auth enforcement, or bypass auth checks. Monitor for successful endpoint access from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — need detection for file-write operations initiated through Splunk service processes that violate expected behavior (creating files outside Splunk directories, truncating system files).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation operations (FileCreate, FileDelete, FileOverwritten events) executed by Splunk/PostgreSQL sidecar processes that write to unexpected locations (outside Splunk_HOME, system directories, /etc/, /var/) or truncate existing files with modifications after hours or from non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Must correlate scanner reports against evidence of actual endpoint access and exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for systems flagged as unpatched for CVE-2026-20253, then cross-reference against web logs and network telemetry for actual exploitation attempts (unauthenticated requests to sidecar endpoints). Alert if scanner shows 'patched' but network evidence shows exploitation attempts post-patch-date.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Endpoint Exposure Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes asset-exposure hunt — must identify all internet-exposed Splunk instances and PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints and verify they enforce authentication before allowing file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Splunk instances accessible from untrusted networks (WAN/internet) on ports commonly used for sidecar endpoints. Verify that connection attempts to these services trigger auth enforcement before allowing I/O operations. Flag any instances that accept unauthenticated connections to file-manipulation endpoints.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Compliance for CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-21' — auditors and regulators will ask about compliance. Must track patch deployment against this deadline across all Splunk deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Weekly query of patch management system and vulnerability scanner for all Splunk Enterprise instances; alert if any system remains unpatched for CVE-2026-20253 past the federal due date (2026-06-21). Track deployment percentage and flag outliers (long tail of late-patching systems).

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253 (versions prior to patch release). suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Exploitation Attempts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected spawning of child processes from PostgreSQL sidecar service. Detect file system operations initiated by sidecar with abnormal privileges or targeting protected directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Manipulation on Splunk Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files.' File creation and truncation events are direct exploitation artifacts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' with CVE substitution instructions. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Splunk Enterprise instances exposed on public networks via scanner results (Qualys, Nessus, native cloud scanners). Flag vulnerability scanner hits for CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference internet-facing Splunk assets against patch inventory; alert on unpatched or unverified instances before federal due date (2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Function Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function' — the attack vector is unauthenticated HTTP access to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints per article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk critical-function endpoints lacking valid authentication (no Authorization header, no session cookie). Baseline normal Splunk API access patterns and alert on high-volume unauthenticated requests or successful requests from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Operations via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is the impact phase and requires direct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/truncation events spawned by Splunk processes (splunkd.exe, splunk-postgresql) outside normal configuration directories. Monitor for child processes of Splunk with FILE_CREATE or FILE_WRITE_TO_DISK access to system-critical paths. Correlate with unauthenticated network requests to detect exploitation in progress.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Requests to PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Core attack surface: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero use cases for initial endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/TCP connections to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar service port from external or unexpected sources, especially unauthenticated payloads. Baseline expected clients; flag any inbound access from untrusted networks lacking valid authentication headers or tokens.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Writes from PostgreSQL Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' No file-system detection use case was generated for sidecar-initiated file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or truncation events originating from Splunk postgresql processes writing outside normal data directories. Alert on writes to /etc, /bin, config paths, or other sensitive locations. Correlate sidecar process spawning with unexpected FileWrite events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms this CVE is actively exploited in CISA KEV. No signature-based or payload-detection use case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy IDS/WAF rules for known CVE-2026-20253 exploitation payloads targeting Splunk sidecar endpoints. Alert on POST/PUT requests with file-creation or file-truncation directives to sidecar service paths.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Patch Lag Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due date 2026-06-21. No compliance or version-detection use case was built.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanner for all Splunk Enterprise instances with versions prior to the first patched release. Flag systems deployed after the federal due date still running vulnerable versions. Correlate scanner gaps with endpoint telemetry showing active Splunk processes.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Port Discovery Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as attack vector. No reconnaissance detection for sidecar port enumeration or service discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on port-scanning, service-probing, or repeated connection attempts to Splunk infrastructure targeting non-standard ports where sidecar services listen, especially from external sources followed by successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar External Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit flows 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' to 'unauthenticated user' — implies network-exposed service; asset-exposure hunt template canonically applies here
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for inbound network connections to Splunk Enterprise systems on the sidecar service port. Verify the service is responding to external/untrusted sources. Cross-reference against asset inventory; flag any instance where PostgreSQL sidecar should be internal-only but has external listeners.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Sidecar Authentication Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article defines vulnerability as 'missing authentication for critical function' — detection must capture requests to vulnerable endpoint without valid auth headers
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/POST requests to Splunk Enterprise sidecar endpoints (typically /services/server/info or similar) originating from external IPs or lacking authentication tokens. Look for multi-attempt patterns suggesting active exploitation or reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Create/Truncate via Splunk Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploit 'could allow...to create or truncate arbitrary files' — file operations initiated by the sidecar service process without legitimate corresponding requests establish exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file create/delete/truncate operations where parent process is Splunk sidecar daemon and target path is outside standard Splunk directories (especially /etc, /opt, /var/log). Correlate with network telemetry showing inbound unauthenticated connections to sidecar within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Configuration File Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation impact: attacker can 'truncate arbitrary files' — critical configs and log files are high-value targets indicating successful compromise
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected modifications to Splunk Enterprise configuration directories (/opt/splunk/etc/), authentication files, or indexed data partitions. Particular emphasis on truncation events (file size drop to zero) or rapid sequential deletes. Cross-correlate with failed auth event spikes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Service Failed Authentication Spike
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated access attempt detection — repeated failed auth to sidecar endpoint is exploitation signature
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk application/auth logs for spike in authentication failures targeting the PostgreSQL sidecar service. Establish baseline for legitimate access patterns. Alert on sustained 401/403 rates from single source IP or subnet. Threshold: >10 failed auth attempts in 5 minutes from same source.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Anything in CISA KEV is currently being exploited' and recommends vulnerability scanner checks for CVE-2026-20253. No asset-exposure use case was generated despite template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances (port 8089, 9997) exposed to untrusted networks or reachable without authentication enforcement. Correlate vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-20253 with external network reachability and patch status.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Unauthorized Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names attack vector: 'unauthenticated user...through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No endpoint-access detection monitoring was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connection attempts to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or custom variants) lacking valid authentication. Alert on successful unauthenticated access or command execution via the sidecar endpoint.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation and Truncation on Splunk Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact as 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' No impact-phase file-manipulation detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise systems for unexpected file creation, modification, or truncation events associated with PostgreSQL sidecar processes or connections to the sidecar endpoint. Baseline expected file I/O and alert on anomalous operations.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match for CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' No scanner-based detection rule was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-20253 across Splunk Enterprise assets. Combine with network exposure telemetry and patch-status data to identify high-risk unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user' accessing 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is the direct exploitation vector. Pipeline missed the core attack path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or alternate) that originate from untrusted sources, lack authentication headers, or bypass auth validation. Correlate with Splunk version detection for CVE-2026-20253 vulnerable builds (pre-patch 2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — no detection UC was generated for this post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and truncation events on Splunk hosts initiated by splunkd or postgres processes in system directories, configuration paths, or data volumes. Baseline normal file operations and alert on anomalous patterns, especially files outside expected Splunk directories.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry implies 'observed exploited in the wild' — T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) mandates detection of exposed Splunk instances. No network-perimeter UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Splunk management port (8089, 8000) and cluster-replication ports (9997+) for external accessibility from untrusted IP ranges. Alert if Splunk management console is reachable from public internet or unintended networks. Cross-reference with patch status for CVE-2026-20253.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Anomalous Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the exploitation channel. No behavioral detection for sidecar abuse patterns was produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar service logs for requests from unexpected network ranges, requests lacking expected authentication tokens, or requests calling file-manipulation functions (CREATE, DROP, TRUNCATE) from unauthenticated contexts. Baseline legitimate sidecar traffic and alert on statistical anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Presence in Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the primary remediation trigger. No asset-inventory or scanner-integration UC was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances with version tags matching CVE-2026-20253 vulnerable versions (pre-patch cut). Flag all unpatched instances with federal deadline 2026-06-21. Escalate any exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets.' Unauthenticated attack requires public-facing instance. No exposure detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Splunk Enterprise instances reachable from untrusted networks (ports 8000, 8089). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20253 presence. Prioritize instances with no WAF/NAC between internet and service.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No detection generated for this specific vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk HTTP logs for requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (/api/v2/postgresql* or similar) lacking valid Authorization header or session cookie that return success codes (200, 201, 204). Baseline legitimate service-to-service traffic.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' No file-system-level detection created for exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or modification in Splunk-owned directories (*/splunk/var/lib/*, */splunk/etc/*) initiated by sidecar service account (splunk-sidecar, postgres user) outside scheduled maintenance windows. Correlate with unauthenticated HTTP access logs in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Missing Authentication to Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article title and description: 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function.' Pipeline missed the authentication-bypass vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to /api/v2/* or /services/* endpoints in Splunk logs where Authorization header is absent or empty AND response code is 2xx. Compare against baseline of legitimate unauthenticated endpoints.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar PostgreSQL Injection Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' enables file operations. Detect abnormal PostgreSQL queries from sidecar for file I/O.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL query logs for COPY, pg_read_file(), pg_write_file() or similar file I/O functions executed from sidecar process context without corresponding Splunk API audit log entry. Flag file paths outside expected data directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE by number. No use case generated to correlate scanner alerts, vulnerability confirmation, or exploitation indicators for this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Upon positive CVE-2026-20253 scan result: review Splunk access logs from past 30 days for unauthenticated sidecar endpoint requests. Check for User-Agent patterns consistent with scanning/exploitation tools. Correlate with failed authentication attempts 24h pre/post scan.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Upload to JCE Component Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'JCE Flaw Allowing PHP Code Execution'—JCE is a file-editor component, making file upload the attack surface. The phrase 'PHP Code Execution' indicates attacker is uploading or injecting executable content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to Joomla JCE component directories (e.g., /components/com_jce/uploads/ or similar) with .php, .phtml, .phar, or double-extension uploads. Alert on successful uploads followed by HTTP GET/POST requests to the uploaded file path, especially with query parameters or POST bodies indicative of payload testing.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt to JCE Component Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: JCE vulnerability is 'actively exploited' per article title—requires HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints. Common vectors involve POST/GET to /index.php?option=com_jce or similar Joomla component invocation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests containing 'com_jce' in query string or POST body, especially with unusual parameter values (base64, hex-encoded payloads), multiple consecutive 5xx responses to the same endpoint, or requests from non-authenticated sessions to sensitive JCE endpoints like upload, media, or file handlers.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Server Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PHP Code Execution'—once JCE exploit succeeds, the web server process (apache, nginx, www-data, IIS AppPool) will execute attacker-controlled PHP. This is direct post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server processes (httpd, apache2, nginx, w3wp.exe) spawning unusual child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, python) or executing commands with high entropy strings, network connections, or file writes outside the web root. Alert on PHP eval(), system(), exec(), passthru(), or shell_exec() calls detected in PHP error logs or caught by WAF/IDS.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence via JCE Upload
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability coupled with file-upload capability is commonly weaponized for persistence via web shell. Phrase 'actively exploited' suggests attackers are achieving stable footholds, not one-shot payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new .php/.phtml/.asp files in web-accessible directories, especially with names common in web shells (shell.php, upload.php, index.html~, .htaccess modifications). Cross-reference with HTTP logs showing repeated access to these files from different source IPs/user-agents, or access patterns inconsistent with normal CMS users (e.g., requests at off-hours, rapid parameter enumeration).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution from Web Context
suggestion.rationale: PHP RCE in JCE allows attacker to execute system commands. Phrase 'actively exploited' implies attackers are going beyond single-payload drops to enumerate, lateral move, or establish C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries, HTTP/HTTPS connections, or reverse-shell callbacks originating from web server processes or PHP child processes. Flag connections to known C2 domains, anomalous outbound ports (4444, 5555, 6666, 8888), or PowerShell/curl/wget processes launched by Apache/IIS with suspicious remote URLs in command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: JCE Component Version Detection via Joomla Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploiting 'actively exploited' flaws typically perform Joomla version/component enumeration first. Detection of this reconnaissance can trigger hunting for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Joomla version/component info endpoints (/administrator/index.php, /index.php?option=com_jce&view=..., /components/com_jce/...., /.htaccess enumeration). Alert on patterns: multiple 404/403 responses to com_jce paths (failed exploitation probing), Access to /administrator or Joomla XML manifests, or User-Agent strings from automated scanners/exploitation frameworks.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Unauthenticated Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exploitation vector and the entry point for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints from external sources completed without valid authentication headers. Alert on successful responses (HTTP 200-299) to sidecar API calls from non-whitelisted IP ranges. Cross-reference against baseline of legitimate admin access patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthorized File Operations via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—file system write operations through the sidecar service initiated by unauthenticated requests warrant behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file create or truncate operations in Splunk config/data directories when originating from the PostgreSQL sidecar service API without corresponding authenticated user session in Splunk audit logs. Flag any file operations in sensitive paths initiated through the sidecar endpoint.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: Federal patch due 2026-06-21, CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation. Standard asset-exposure hunt referenced in article templates but missing from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Splunk Enterprise instances with unpatched CVE-2026-20253 after federal due date. Correlate with network exposure scans to identify internet-facing instances. Cross-reference patch management records for remediation status.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Unexpected Service Port Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies exploitation through 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—external traffic to internal auxiliary service ports is inherently anomalous and warrants network-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound traffic from external/untrusted IP ranges to Splunk sidecar service ports. Look for HTTP methods (POST/PUT) targeting sidecar endpoints with payloads indicating file manipulation intent (create/truncate operations).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — core initial-access vector. Pipeline missed detection for unauthorized requests to this critical internal service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints lacking authentication tokens or valid sessions. Focus on POST/PUT requests from untrusted IPs or external sources attempting to trigger file operations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'could allow creation or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct impact mechanism. Detection should catch file I/O anomalies from the sidecar process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation/truncation on Splunk systems initiated by or routed through the PostgreSQL sidecar. Alert on modifications to system files, logs, or recovery mechanisms outside expected Splunk data directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit CVE identifier for correlation with scanner output. Standard CISA KEV practice to flag positive detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any positive CVE-2026-20253 detections in vulnerability scanner results. Correlate timing with web access logs to identify if scanning activity aligns with exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Exposure Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Detection should identify unpatched Splunk Enterprise instances, especially externally accessible ones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise deployments. Cross-reference patch dates against 2026-06-21 deadline. Alert on instances accessible from DMZ or untrusted networks running pre-patch versions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt — PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the attack vector; pipeline surfaced no detection logic for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or internal service ports). Flag access attempts from non-trusted sources, especially external IPs. Correlate with missing authentication logs or failed credential validation events on the sidecar service.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Operations via PostgreSQL Sidecar (CVE-2026-20253 Impact)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow creation or truncation of arbitrary files.' Pipeline missed detection of the exploitation outcome—file operations via unauthenticated endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation operations originating from PostgreSQL sidecar processes when preceded by unauthenticated access. Unusual file write/delete patterns in Splunk directories or config paths without corresponding authenticated sessions warrant immediate review.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure — Unpatched Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...Substitute this CVE wherever the template references CVE.' Pipeline failed to instantiate exposure baseline. Federal patch due 2026-06-21; this is a time-sensitive compliance gate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Splunk Enterprise instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference patch-management and asset databases to identify unpatched systems. Alert on exposed instances (internet-facing, no network segmentation) with confirmed vulnerability signatures or version mismatches.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Functions (Authentication Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'missing authentication for critical function.' Pipeline did not generate detection for bypass of authentication controls or access to protected endpoints without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk and PostgreSQL logs for requests to critical service endpoints (sidecar API, file management endpoints) lacking authentication tokens or credentials. Flag 'unauthenticated' or 'unauthorized' status codes followed by successful command execution on file operations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the primary exploitation vector and baseline deviation is high-confidence signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Splunk sidecar endpoint requests (port ranges 8088–9998, typical URIs) and expected authentication headers (Authorization, X-Splunk-Auth). Alert on requests to sidecar endpoints lacking auth headers or originating from unexpected sources (non-management IP ranges, external IPs). High-fidelity if request body contains file paths or sidecar-specific commands.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write or Truncation by Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' File-system event is impact indicator distinguishing reconnaissance from successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk daemon processes (splunkd, splunk-optimize) for CreateFile or WriteFile events outside expected deployment directories (e.g., sudden writes to /etc, /var/log, Windows System32, or Splunk's own config/log paths with 0-byte truncation). Post-exploitation truncation of audit logs or credentials files is highest fidelity.

suggestion.title: Network Scanning for Splunk Service Ports Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor reconnaissance phase preceding CVE-2026-20253 exploitation; early detection of scanning activity enables interception.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential connection attempts to multiple known Splunk service ports (8000, 8001, 8089, 9997, 9998) from single source within 5-minute window, or attempts to random/ephemeral ports associated with sidecar services. Baseline legitimate scanning windows (e.g., scheduled vulnerability scans from known IPs) to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Payload Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designates active wild exploitation; WAF/proxy signatures for known payload patterns are available and should be deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy network-based IDS/WAF rules matching known CVE-2026-20253 exploitation signatures (specific sidecar URI paths, query string injection patterns, HTTP method abuse). Alert on any match; correlate with file-system and process events to confirm successful exploitation vs. benign scanner activity.

suggestion.title: Splunk Daemon Restart or Crash Post-File Truncation
suggestion.rationale: File truncation can corrupt Splunk configuration or bootstrap files, triggering process crashes or unexpected restarts; temporal correlation is high-confidence compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Splunk lifecycle (average startup time, expected child processes). Alert on unexpected process termination events within 30 seconds of anomalous file truncation, or rapid respawn loops (3+ restarts in 5 minutes). Cross-correlate file events and process events for end-to-end exploitation chain.
